claim: Code skills are deterministic: same inputs produce same outputs, enabling traditional software testing and verification
source: SoK: Agentic Skills — Beyond Tool Use in LLM Agents, arXiv 2602.20867, Jiang et al., 2026-02-24 (7 authors)
evidence: Retrieved arXiv abstract page and full HTML text (119,465 chars). The sentence appears verbatim in the body: 'The key advantage of code skills is determinism: given the same inputs, a code skill produces the same outputs, enabling traditional software testing and verification.' Note the ABSTRACT does not contain this claim; it is in the Pattern-2 (executable code skills) discussion
consequence: Section 4.8's determinism observation is PRIOR ART, not a finding of this work. Must be reframed as citation

consequence: Directly relevant to the assertions-vs-prose argument and strengthens it, but means the general form of that argument is also known

claim: POPPER applies rigorous statistical validation to agent-generated hypotheses
source: arXiv 2502.09858 (identifier from web search, NOT yet confirmed)
evidence: Retrieved on retry: arXiv 2502.09858, 'Automated Hypothesis Validation with Agentic Sequential Falsifications', 2025-02-14, Huang K, Jin Y, Li R, Li MY, Candes E, Leskovec J. Full 65-page PDF parsed (209,851 chars). POPPER converts p-values to e-values and aggregates them in a sequential testing framework with strict Type-I error control; its gate on which experiments run is an LLM-as-a-judge relevance checker, which the authors report agrees imperfectly with human evaluators (77% human pass rate) and needs further domain-specific expertise. The strings assert, guardrail, reusable and skill library occur ZERO times in the paper
consequence: Novelty claim SURVIVES and is now specific: POPPER controls the inferential procedure across tests with a model-mediated gate; the assertions here constrain the validity of a single measurement in code, before any statistic is computed. Section 2 now states this as a verified comparison and notes the two are complementary
